summary: Grise Fiord Airport (YGZ) is a small remote airport serving the Inuit hamlet of Grise Fiord on southern Ellesmere Island in Nunavut, Canada. As one of the northernmost civilian airports in the country, it provides a vital lifeline for the isolated community of approximately 130 residents, where there are no road connections to the outside world. The airport operates under extreme Arctic conditions and primarily handles small turboprop aircraft on flights connecting to Resolute Bay and other regional hubs.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly to Grise Fiord Airport?
A: Canadian North is the main carrier serving Grise Fiord with scheduled turboprop flights, primarily connecting through Resolute Bay. Charter flights may also operate depending on community needs and weather conditions.

Q: How far is Grise Fiord from the North Pole?
A: Grise Fiord is located at about 76°N latitude, making it roughly 1,500 km (930 miles) south of the North Pole. It is one of the northernmost permanently inhabited communities in Canada.

Q: When is the airport operational?
A: The airport operates year-round but is subject to weather disruptions, particularly during the long Arctic winter when polar night, extreme cold, and blowing snow can affect flight schedules.

Q: Is there a road to Grise Fiord?
A: No, there are no roads connecting Grise Fiord to other communities. The hamlet is accessible only by air or, seasonally, by sea when ice conditions permit.
